items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: you are doing a road trip here with the trio of Joseph Daley and Scott Robinson

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Well see now even people like John Cage for instance, definitely had a framework. But he wanted you to infuse your ideas into that framework. And I remember oh man, it was really weird. We were in the University of Illinois and Cage was there one day. And you know you’re playing all this weird music, and some of it was written you know but he’d tell you to do something, and I did something unusual and I’m looking at him down there at his seat. And I did it. And he like had an orgasm, like that, some…

So I’ve been thinking about this, I watched a few things on YouTube that you were on, and then some other things that Joseph Daley had done. I was trying to surmise if listening to avante garde or free or extremely creative music is easier for people who don’t know how music works? Because I think I have a bad habit of trying to compartmentalize things if I’m listening to something, and I’m listening — okay I’ve got the groove or I can hear the key, I can hear the root. And then if music comes along that it’s not…

No, I understand that inquiry because you have to get over I guess a feeling of rejection of the ideas that you present, the fear of that. You know what I mean? Because if you only want to please people then you are limited by what would please them. But sometimes my way of thinking is that you throw something at people that they don’t © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: I’m not just playing anything at any time and Warren is not just playing anything at any time. It’s stuff that, you know that we’re working to build ensemble experiences.

ctx.x: Right. Last night we played in this space, I can see the tympani behind you.
Yeah, tremendously played by Warren Smith, one of the great tympanists. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

It’s interesting because at some point I was, while you were playing, I was, on occasion I’d close my eyes and just do the ear thing. And I was hearing these sounds, like is that coming from the tympani?
